repairs.before_quote: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited through the Poincaré supplier named below, together with Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, nonempty and bounded in one direction, let $L$ and $a$ be as in [[def-uniformly-elliptic-divergence-form-operator]] with ellipticity constant $\theta$, coefficient bounds $M_a,M_b,M_c$ (with the componentwise drift bounds $|b^i|\le M_b$), and let $C_P$ be the Poincar\'e constant of [[thm-poincare-inequality-for-w-one-p-zero]] for $p=2$. Assume the explicit smallness condition $$\theta-\sqrt n\,C_PM_b-C_P^2M_c>0 .$$ Then for every $F\in H^{-1}(\Omega)$ there is a unique weak solution $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ of $Lu=F$ ([[def-weak-dirichlet-solution-for-a-divergence-form-operator]]), and with $\alpha_0:=\theta-\sqrt n\,C_PM_b-C_P^2M_c$ it satisfies $$\|u\|_{H^1_0}\le\frac{1+C_P^2}{\alpha_0}\|F\|_{H^{-1}} .$$ When $b\equiv0$ the condition reduces to $M_c<\theta/C_P^2$, the sign/smallness condition of the plan; in the model case $a^{ij}=\delta^{ij}$, $b=0$, $c=0$ it gives $\alpha_0=1$ and gives existence and uniqueness for the zero-boundary weak Poisson problem.

repairs.before_quote:
Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, with $H^1_0(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ the zero-boundary Sobolev space $W^{1,2}_0$ over $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]], [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]]). Define
$$H^{-1}(\Omega):=\{\,F:H^1_0(\Omega)\to\mathbb K : F\text{ is bounded and conjugate-linear}\,\},$$
with
$$\|F\|_{H^{-1}}:=\sup_{\|v\|_{H^1_0}\le1}|F(v)| .$$
**Pairing convention.** The pairing $\langle F,v\rangle:=F(v)$ is linear in $F$ and conjugate-linear in $v$; it is the dual pairing of $H^{-1}(\Omega)$ with $H^1_0(\Omega)$, not the $L^2$ inner product. The map $F\mapsto\overline{F(\cdot)}$ is an isometric conjugate-linear bijection of $H^{-1}(\Omega)$ onto the Banach dual $(H^1_0(\Omega))^*$ of [[def-dual-space-of-a-normed-space]] ([[def-operator-norm]], [[def-space-of-bounded-linear-operators]]); the design's notation $(H^1_0)^*$ is read through this identification, which is the one compatible with the page's sesquilinear convention (linear in the first argument, conjugate-linear in the second) fixed in [[def-bounded-coercive-and-symmetric-sesquilinear-forms]]. The space $H^{-1}(\Omega)$ is a normed space, complete because $(H^1_0(\Omega))^*$ is complete and $\overline{F(\cdot)}$ is an isometry in both directions ([[thm-bounded-operator-space-is-banach]], [[def-complex-conjugate-real-imaginary-part-and-modulus]]). For $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ the map $v\mapsto(f,v)_{L^2}$ is the corresponding element of $H^{-1}(\Omega)$ under the conventions of [[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]] and [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]], where complex integrability is in the sense of the latter; identifying a general element of $H^{-1}$ with an $L^2$ function is an embedding statement, never a definition. No element of $H^{-1}$ is a distribution here: it acts on Sobolev classes by the given pairing.

repairs.reason: The consumer states CC and AC and n>=1, a bounded interval or C1 domain, real coefficients, a real form and real datum f in L2. Its reaction Lambda(v)=a(u,v)-integral fv is real linear on H1_0, hence conjugate-linear under the real specialization. Boundedness of the form gives |Lambda(v)|<=(M ||u||_H1+||f||_2)||v||_H1_0 by Cauchy-Schwarz and ||v||_2<=||v||_H1_0, using the full H1 norm. Thus it is an H-minus-one functional. Step 2.1 uses this continuity clause for Sobolev tests already shown to be in H1_0, and the obstacle inequality independently supplies positivity for every nonnegative H1_0 competitor. The changed final definition sentence permits smooth-test distribution identification without changing the bounded-functional/global-test interface. It does not permit an arbitrary L1-local datum on arbitrary H1_0 tests.
